newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Paranapanema to raise tin output max 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Paranapanema to raise tin output max 15 pct.

text.p: Brazilian metals company Paranapanema expects to see a rise in the company's tin output to between 17,000 and 18,000 tonnes in 1997 against 15,600 tonnes in 1996, the commercial director said.

But there is no question of the company producing 8,000 tonnes next year more than in 1996 as suggested in a recent speech by RMT Metals' Robert Goldsobel to an industry conference, Antonio Aranha Andrade said.
"We have been telling our clients all along our production is going to be 15,600 tonnes this year and between 17,000 to 18,000 in 1997," Andrade said.
Paranapanema's output currently accounts for around 80 percent of national production and 12 percent of international consumption.
Internal sales in 1997 are expected to grow slightly to 3,600 to 3,800 tonnes from current levels of 3,300 to 3,500 tonnes.
Exports to the U.S. should remain on the same level of around 9,000 tonnes while South American sales are seen rising to between 1,000 to 1,200 tonnes from 800 to 1,000 tonnes.
The main difference next year is that Paranapanema is hoping to make a return to the European market after a virtual absence of two years, with target sales in 1997 of around 3,000 tonnes.
The company is still looking to boost annual production to 25,000 tonnes by the year 2002 but increases in production will be cautious so as not to affect international prices.
"We will take great care with the market," Andrade said.

In Goldsobel's speech, the trader predicted a possible 25 percent fall in international tin prices over the next six months due to rising world production although this was working on the basis of an 8,000 tonne rise in Paranapanema's output.

Other increases were expected from Indonesia's P.T. Timah to over 40,000 tonnes and Australian Group Koba Tin, also mining and smelting in Indonesia, to 12,000 tonnes from current levels of 7,000 tonnes also in the next 18 months.
China and Peru are also seen contributing to greater availability, the trader said.
A group of U.S. traders today predicted tin prices in the first half 1997 are set to remain at current levels or barely move above this year's highs at best.

RMT Metals and Paranapanema were at opposite ends of the table when it came to price predictions, with RMT Metals seeing levels between $5,400 and $6,150 while Paranapanema instead expected prices to rise to between $6,450 and $6,850.
LME cash tin settled at $5,820 a tonne Monday, near the day's lows.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
